title: Nodes That Hold Contracts
objective: After this lesson you will be able to write node functions with typed inputs and contract-shaped outputs, validate at node boundaries with quarantine discipline, and handle node failure (retry, fallback, escalate) explicitly.
why: Nodes are where prompts meet production: a triage node returns a *string* instead of the enum, a draft node exceeds length, a lookup returns null. Unvalidated node outputs corrupt shared state silently — every downstream node inherits the lie. Contract-holding nodes (validate in, validate out, fail loudly with evidence) turn integration bugs into caught exceptions.

blocks.text: Nodes are functions with contracts, not prompts with hopes

A production node has three parts: **prompt** (the Prompt 101 pack piece), **call** (model with bounded retries/timeouts), **validate** (schema-check the output before it touches state). The validate step is non-negotiable: node outputs are untrusted input to the graph, exactly like user input to an API. Zod-style schemas (or hand validators in the playground) enforce enums, types, and bounds at the boundary.

blocks.caption: Validate out: enums, types, bounds — quarantine with evidence on violation

blocks.text: Nodes fail three ways, each with a designed response. **Transient** (timeout, rate limit): bounded retries with backoff, then escalate — never infinite loops. **Invalid output** (schema violation): one repair retry with the error quoted back, then quarantine. **Downstream missing** (lookup null): fallback values or explicit unknown-paths, never invented data. Undesigned failure modes become silent corruption; designed ones become log entries.

blocks.caption: Two tries with evidence, then quarantine — bounded, never infinite

blocks.text: Retries, replays, and resume-after-crash re-execute nodes — so nodes must be **idempotent**: same state in, same update out, no duplicate side effects. Pure compute nodes (classify, draft) are naturally safe; side-effecting nodes (send email, issue refund) need idempotency keys and check-before-act guards. A node unsafe to re-run is a node unsafe to operate.

blocks.title: Validate the node output
blocks.note: Run it: expect ok, bad-enum, bad-confidence, not-an-object — in order. Each rejection names its rule: validators that explain themselves make quarantine logs self-diagnosing.

items: Nodes = prompt + bounded call + boundary validation; outputs are untrusted input to the graph
Failures designed: transient→bounded retry, invalid→quoted repair then quarantine, missing→fallback/unknown
Idempotency required: retries and replays re-execute nodes — side effects need keys and guards

exercise.prompt: (a) Run the practice validator and map each case to its rule. (b) Extend it with a reason field rule (string, ≤12 words — count words, not chars) plus a test. (c) Sketch the idempotency guard for a refund-issue node (key check + check-before-act) in three lines of pseudocode.
hints: Mapping: ok / bad-enum:Exchange / bad-confidence:'high' / not-an-object. Each names rule + value.
Reason rule: typeof string, split(/\s+/).length <= 12, else 'bad-reason-length'. Test with 13-word reason.
Guard: if (state.refundIssued[key]) return {}; const r = lookup(key); if (r.settled) return {refundIssued:{[key]:true}}; issue(key).
exercise.why: Boundary validation (typed rules with evidence), contract extension (new field, new test), and side-effect safety (keys + guards) are the three node disciplines — each practiced, none merely read.
exercise.code: // Rule-addition pattern: type check + bound check + named error + test case.

options: Quarantine with evidence (bad enum + raw) — downstream reads only validated updates
quiz.explain: Boundary validation: unlisted labels corrupt routers and switches. Quarantine preserves evidence for repair-or-escalate; silent coercion lies downstream.

quiz.q: Timeout on first call, success on retry. Design principle?
options: Bounded retries with backoff, then escalate — transient failures get chances, not eternities
quiz.explain: Bounded retry converts transients into successes and persistents into logged escalations. Unbounded retry converts incidents into hangs.

quiz.q: Refund node re-runs after a crash and double-issues. Missing?
options: Idempotency: keys + check-before-act so re-execution is safe
quiz.explain: Retries, replays, and resumes re-execute nodes. Side effects without keys double-apply — idempotency is an operability requirement, not polish.

summary: Contract-holding nodes validate in and out, fail by design (retry/fallback/escalate with evidence), and re-run safely. Integration bugs die at boundaries.
next: Workers contracted — now the traffic system: conditional edges, routing tables, and branch coverage for graphs. Next: routers with tests.
